The italic any of answers to no source morpheme. Rule 15's supplied quantifying determiner reaches a word standing in the slot where an a or a the would stand before a noun carrying no determiner of its own, and here the ASV writes its own supplied the after any, so any heads a partitive phrase rather than determining the nominal expression; no מִן stands in the clause, and the chain's own of is אֶפְרַיִם's under rule 19. The supplied quantifier and its supplied preposition stand together and do one office, so they are one added unit under rules 2 and 30, exactly as rule 33 makes a supplied noun with its supplied preposition one added unit; headed on any, the word carrying its force. The competing reading, taken by the earlier alignment, folds any of into the construct noun's unit as a supplied determiner under rule 15.

review_notes: Corrected one unit: the italic any of is now its own added unit rather than a supplied determiner inside פְּלִיטֵי's unit. Rule 15's supplied determiner stands where an a or a the would stand before a noun with no determiner of its own, and here the ASV writes a supplied the of its own after any, so the partitive quantifier and its of answer to no morpheme; they stand together and do one office, so they form one added unit (rules 2, 30, 33), headed on any.
The construct noun keeps the supplied the under rule 29 and heads on fugitives (rules 24, 31); the chain's of is אֶפְרַיִם's under rule 19.

Everything else stands: the marginal Or, toward Ephraim is read and set aside (rule 38); הָיָה takes it was so that because the that stands inside the frame ahead of the כִּי clause, which leaves the apodosis waw unrepresented (rule 45); and the interrogative particle takes the fronted Art while אַתָּה keeps only thou (rules 17, 20).
